question: ______ connect India's four big metro cities of Delhi-Mumbai-Chennai-Kolkata.
solution:
The correct answer is__** Golden Quadrilateral.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Golden Quadrilateral:-**

 
 
• It is a highway network connecting the major cities of Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata.
 
• It is a part of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP) and was completed in 2012.
 
• The Golden Quadrilateral covers a distance of 5,846 km and is one of the longest highways in the world.
 
• The project was initiated by the government to improve the transportation infrastructure in the country and boost economic growth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** North-South Corridor of NHDP:-**

 
 
• It is a different highway project that connects Srinagar in the north to Kanyakumari in the south.
 
 
 
• **National Highway 44:-**
 
 
• It connects Srinagar to Kanyakumari via Delhi.
 
 
 
• **National Highway 47A:-**
 
 
• It connects Salem to Kochi in the south.
